title: Go SDK: cooperative stream pause-handshake and graceful drain safety
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Add a cooperative pause/resume handshake and explicit graceful-drain semantics to the Go SDK streaming client so applications can: (1) pause a consuming loop to finish processing inflight messages without losing order, (2) resume from a well-defined checkpoint, and (3) signal cooperative cancellation reasons (client-requested drain vs network/fatal).

Why this work: Current streaming ergonomics make it hard for application code to implement safe shutdowns and in-flight message processing guarantees while using context cancellation. We want an explicit protocol and Go-level ergonomic primitives that: provide deterministic checkpoints (per-message sequence ids), avoid goroutine leaks, reduce races between context.Done and message reads, and interoperate with server-side graceful-drain frames.

Scope of changes:
- Protocol: define two new control frames for the wire protocol: PAUSE_REQUEST(seq_id) and PAUSE_ACK(seq_id). Client sends PAUSE_REQUEST with last-seen seq; server responds with PAUSE_ACK after ensuring the KV/cache state and any required flush. Also a GRACEFUL_DRAIN(reason) frame initiated by client or server. (Protocol spec sketch appended to PR).
- Go SDK API surface: add Stream.Pause(ctx, timeout) (returns checkpoint seq string) and Stream.Resume(ctx, seq) helpers. Implement Stream.CloseWithDrain(ctx, reason) which attempts cooperative drain before hard close.
- Internal: implement a single-shot pauseCoord channel per connection to serialize pause handshakes, and move stream read loop to a select on {dataCh, controlCh, ctx.Done()} with clear semantics so ctx cancellations set an explicit CancelReason error type and do not silently drop unacknowledged messages.
- Tests: high-fidelity integration tests simulating (a) client pause while processing long handler, (b) network partition during PAUSE handshake, (c) server-initiated drain. Load tests with 5k concurrent streams to verify no goroutine leak regression.

Decision notes and trade-offs:
- We debated automatic checkpointing on every message vs explicit checkpoint API. Chose explicit checkpointing to avoid perf regressions for high-throughput low-latency streams; most client apps want control when to checkpoint.
- We considered embedding the pause handshake into context cancellation (i.e., context carries checkpoint), but that made ergonomics hard and leaked protocol details via context. Instead we provide small helpers that accept contexts for timeouts.
- Implementation will prefer channels + atomic state rather than heavy mutexing to keep latency low. Coordinating pause handshakes is serialized per-connection to avoid complex interleavings.

PRs and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Go+Stream+Pause+Handshake (early draft)
- Implementation draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4782 (WIP)
- Bench: microbench shows ~0.6% p50 token latency overhead under pause-enabled builds and no measurable p99 uplift after optimizations (details in PR bench/ folder).

Open tasks / next steps:
- Finish server-side GRACEFUL_DRAIN handling and coordinate with runtime team (owner: Priya Rao).
- Add convenience Example in SDK docs: example that shows graceful shutdown of an HTTP service that proxies to a stream and waits for Stream.Pause checkpoint before returning 200.
- Add signal handler pattern to examples for SIGTERM that uses Stream.CloseWithDrain with 10s timeout.
- Follow-up to audit all existing stream consumer code for assumptions about message ownership and to update migration notes.

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: new wire frames increase compatibility complexity with older runtime nodes. Mitigation: handshake is opt-in per connection using capability bit; server will ignore unknown frames and respond with NACK to older clients. Backcompat tests included.
- Risk: subtle deadlocks if application repeatedly calls Pause without awaiting ack. Mitigation: Pause API enforces single inflight Pause per stream and returns ErrPauseInProgress if retried.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests covering pause success, pause timeout, network drop during handshake, and resume semantics.
- No goroutine leaks in 5k streams soak test.
- Example added to SDK README and a short howto in Console docs.
- Documentation on migration and opt-in capability flag.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial RFC merged into google doc; scoped feature set to Pause/Resume + CloseWithDrain; mapped owner responsibilities.
2026-03-04: Spike completed comparing channels vs mutex approach; channels chosen for lower latency in read hot-path. See bench notes in PR.
2026-03-06: Prototype Pause/ACK wire frames implemented against local test server; found race when ctx canceled during ack wait — fixed by serializing pauseCoord via single goroutine.
2026-03-09: Integration tests added for server-initiated GRACEFUL_DRAIN; found server behavior differences with older runtime nodes; added capability bit fallback and NACK handling.
